title: Lower Bound
statement:
Given a sorted array of N integers (may contain duplicates) and a target T, find the **lower bound** — the index of the first element that is **greater than or equal to** T.

If all elements are less than T, return N (off-the-end index).

Implement using binary search in O(log N).
inputFormat:
Line 1: two integers N and T.
Line 2: N space-separated integers in non-decreasing order.
outputFormat: A single integer: the 0-indexed lower bound position.
constraints:
1 <= N <= 10^7
-10^9 <= A[i] <= 10^9
Array is sorted in non-decreasing order.
-10^9 <= T <= 10^9

examples.explanation: First index where A[i] >= 5 is index 4.
No element is >= 6, so return N=5.
